extracted.intended_audience: BBC content producers, editors, journalists and production staff
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial standards for achieving 'due accuracy' across BBC output, including sourcing, corroboration, error correction, mandatory referral procedures and oversight of AI. Applies to news, current affairs and other genres with guidance on differing accuracy expectations by format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due accuracy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC is committed to achieving due accuracy in all its output. 'Due' means accuracy must be adequate and appropriate to the output, taking account of the subject and nature of the content, the likely audience expectation and any additional information provided by the BBC that may influence that expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a fundamental editorial obligation underpinning reputation and audience trust. Footnote: relates to Ofcom Broadcasting Code section 5; the BBC applies 'due accuracy' to all output and thereby exceeds that requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy appropriate to genre and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The due accuracy required of, for example, drama, entertainment and comedy, will not usually be the same as for most factual content. The requirements may even vary within a genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers must vary accuracy standards according to format — e.g., factual entertainment, historical documentary, current affairs or news may each demand different levels of corroboration and precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisational duty to ensure accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC must do all it can to ensure due accuracy in all its output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative, organisation-wide obligation (3.2.1) that places responsibility on all involved in creating output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing, evidence and corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: All BBC output, as appropriate to its subject and nature, must be well sourced, based on sound evidence, and where possible corroborated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content producers should be honest and open about what they don't know and avoid unfounded speculation. Claims, allegations, material facts and other content that cannot be corroborated should normally be attributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of unfounded speculation and transparent unknowns
rubrics_metrics.description: Content producers should be honest and open about what they don't know and avoid unfounded speculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When facts cannot be corroborated, attribute the material rather than present it as established fact; be transparent about uncertainties to maintain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: No knowingly or materially misleading content
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC must not knowingly and materially mislead its audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content producers should not distort known facts, present invented material as fact or otherwise undermine audiences' trust in the BBC's content (3.2.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of serious factual errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Serious factual errors should normally be acknowledged and corrected quickly, clearly and appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a serious inaccuracy is identified, the response should be prompt and proportionate to the severity and prominence of the error (3.2.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of accuracy over speed in news/current affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: In news and current affairs content, achieving due accuracy is more important than speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When there is a conflict between being first and being accurate in news/current affairs, accuracy must take precedence (3.2.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory referrals must be made in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory referrals are an essential part of the BBC's editorial and compliance process and must be observed. Mandatory referrals must be referred in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers must stop and refer eligible matters before broadcasting/commissioning — referrals are non-optional and intended to manage legal/editorial risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral for reliance on single unnamed source or anonymity for serious allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to rely on a single unnamed source making a serious allegation or to grant anonymity to a significant contributor making a serious allegation must be referred to Director Editorial Policy and Standards and Programme Legal Advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance referral is required to assess legal and editorial implications (see 3.4.21 for further detail).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral if a potentially defamatory inaccuracy is broadcast
rubrics_metrics.description: Where content producers believe they have broadcast a defamatory inaccuracy, Programme Legal Advice must be consulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult legal advice promptly to manage potential defamation exposure and remedial steps (see 3.4.34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification for output about Northern Ireland and Republic of Ireland projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Content producers intending to produce output about Northern Ireland or significant projects involving the Republic of Ireland should notify Director Northern Ireland of their proposals at an early stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, producers creating material dealing with significant national or regional issues about England, Scotland and Wales who are not based in the relevant nation should inform that nation's director (see 3.4.37). This ensures appropriate editorial oversight and local context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior editorial accountability for AI deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: A senior editorial figure must be responsible and accountable for overseeing the deployment and continuing use of any Artificial Intelligence (AI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should seek advice from Editorial Policy, which may consult the AI Risk Advisory Group, before any decision to deploy the AI. For independent production companies, a senior editorial figure responsible for compliance within the production team should be responsible and accountable for its use of AI (see 3.4.27).
